name: nGZSceneGraph::cStringPool::Instance
notes: Lane OX (scenegraph D1a): nGZSceneGraph::cStringPool is our class (src/sg/cStringPool.h): the scene graph's interned-string table (cIStringPool, 14 slots), with its own std::unordered_map, handle vector and free list in place of the game's MSVC hash-table internals and scratch key (nothing but the pool's own slots reaches them). Hooked: the getter 0xadf8b0 (the function-local static; cSceneGraphSystem's Init / Shutdown / GetStringPool reach the pool only through it), so the game's constructor, destructor, vtable 0xe7c844, every slot body, the handle iterator's vtable 0xe7c880 and the hash-table code only the pool calls are never reached (their entries here, in effect through callers). Tests (tests/sg_string_pool.cpp): SG_StringPool_Slots (120 seeds: each side's pool, the game's built by 0xadf120 in a zeroed block, ours by our constructor; the same seeded run of every slot through each object's own vtable, every answer compared, the handle iterators walked, cloned, compared and released, then the pool destroyed through slot 13), SG_StringPool_Instance (the getter answers one started-by-nobody object, the same each call), SG_StringPool_Hash (0x98bff0, 20000 buffers). mutants 18/19 killed (build/ox_pool_mutants.json, tools/mutate.py): hash shifts and length, iterator skip and IsEqual, QI, case folding, free-list order, release count, empty text, Crc32 flag, Shutdown, AddRefHandle, GetHandles start, empty key, hash seed, GetLength; the survivor (Find without the started check) is equivalent: the table only fills through Intern, which needs the started flag, and Shutdown empties it, so a pool not started has every handle out of range

name: nGZSceneGraph::JenkinsHash
notes: Lane OX: Bob Jenkins' lookup2 hash (__cdecl data, length, seed), the pool's key hash; cShader and the material attribute classes hash names with it too (15 callers), so it is hooked (504 bytes). SG_StringPool_Hash: 20000 random buffers, every tail length 0-11 and lengths past several 12-byte blocks, seeds 0 and random; the slot test hashes through it too. mutants 18/19 killed (build/ox_pool_mutants.json, tools/mutate.py): hash shifts and length, iterator skip and IsEqual, QI, case folding, free-list order, release count, empty text, Crc32 flag, Shutdown, AddRefHandle, GetHandles start, empty key, hash seed, GetLength; the survivor (Find without the started check) is equivalent: the table only fills through Intern, which needs the started flag, and Shutdown empties it, so a pool not started has every handle out of range

name: nGZSceneGraph::cStringPool::StaticDestroy
notes: Lane OX, class: 0xadf8b0's entry. The exit thunk the game's getter registers (destroys the static at 0x10f8c70); registered only by the original getter, so nothing reaches it once the getter is ours. Ours is the compiler's exit code for our function-local static (the destructor 0xadf460 it runs is verified). Not verified: no test runs the thunk (10 bytes: loads the static, jumps to 0xadf460).
